title: Contributing and building Quickque
description: Set up the repository, run the browser and native checks, and contribute without confusing preview behavior with Mac verification.
body:
# Contributing and building Quickque

Quickque welcomes careful, reproducible contributions. Keep the project local-first: do not add cloud script storage, account requirements, API keys, silent transcription fallbacks, or claims that a browser preview proves native behavior. Read the source and tests before changing a workflow, then describe what you actually verified.

## Before you begin

For the repository and browser work, use Node.js 24 and pnpm 10.26.1. For native Mac work, also use an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 14 or newer, Xcode 16 and Swift 6, and the stable Rust toolchain. Intel Macs, Windows, and Linux can be useful for source inspection or platform-neutral checks, but they do not verify the native app, CoreML, microphone, window, signing, or phone behavior.

The public source is [rossboyd/quickque](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque). Clone it and install from the repository root:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque.git
cd quickque
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

## Steps

### Browser development

1. Start the Quickque browser route with the supported development configuration.

   ```shell
   PORT=5173 BASE_PATH=/ pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque dev
   ```

2. Use the browser for manual library, editor, import, **Export Full Backup**/**Import Backup JSON**, and playback work. Treat native-only notices as part of the product contract: browser bridge calls do not create a Mac overlay, Flow helper, or Phone Remote server.

3. Keep browser storage boundaries in mind when testing persistence. A browser origin and the Tauri app use separate localStorage.

### Checks and native commands

1. Run the package typecheck from the repository root when TypeScript changes are involved.

   ```shell
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque typecheck
   ```

2. Run focused tests for the areas you changed.

   ```shell
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque test:document-import
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque test:flow
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque test:remote
   sh tests/remote-protocol/run.sh
   ```

3. On a supported Mac, the native helper and app commands are available through the package scripts:

   ```shell
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque native:test
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque native:build
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque desktop:dev
   pnpm --filter @workspace/quickque desktop:build
   ```

   `desktop:dev` and `desktop:build` run the native helper build first. `desktop:build` also runs the native layout test and creates release artifacts, but neither a local build nor a Linux check is a release-signing, notarization, microphone, overlay, or physical-phone result.

4. For document-import changes, preserve the local worker boundary, size limits, parser notices, and no-network behavior. For Flow changes, preserve explicit model download, offline inference, transient audio/transcript handling, English-only scope, and the native 30-second silence stop. For remote changes, preserve approval, five-minute pairing expiry, trusted-LAN HTTP warning, one-controller rule, and no automatic IP-change recovery.

### Contribute a change

1. Read the relevant source before editing. Useful entry points include [`library.tsx`](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/src/pages/library.tsx), [`reader.tsx`](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/src/pages/reader.tsx), [`settings-dialog.tsx`](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/src/components/settings-dialog.tsx), [`document-import-dialog.tsx`](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/src/components/document-import-dialog.tsx), [`remote-control-dialog.tsx`](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/src/components/remote-control-dialog.tsx), and [`DESKTOP.md`](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/DESKTOP.md).

2. Keep user-facing labels and error states practical. If a behavior is native-only or unverified, say so. Do not turn an automated test result into a Mac claim.

3. Add or update focused tests for the behavior. Record the command, platform, and meaningful result in your pull request. Never include script text, pairing URLs, controller tokens, microphone audio, or transcripts in fixtures or reports.

4. Check licenses before changing dependencies or model integration. Quickque-owned code and documentation use the project MIT license; FluidAudio, parser dependencies, and downloaded model weights retain their own terms. Parakeet weights use the NVIDIA Open Model License, not MIT.

5. Submit a focused pull request to [rossboyd/quickque](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque). Explain what changed, what you tested, what you could not test, and any follow-up needed on a physical Mac or phone.

## Expected result

A contributor can reproduce the browser route, run focused source checks, and distinguish platform-neutral evidence from Mac-only verification. Native commands remain available to supported Mac contributors without claiming that they passed here. Changes preserve local storage, privacy, pairing, and offline boundaries.

## Troubleshooting

- **`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on Mac:** verify pnpm 10.26.1 and the committed lockfile are in use. The workspace retains Darwin packages for documented Mac builds while excluding unsupported non-Darwin optional binaries; do not add an untracked workaround.
- **The browser route requires environment variables:** use `PORT=5173 BASE_PATH=/` exactly for this development route. Desktop Vite uses its own local port and does not use the browser preview variables.
- **A native command cannot run on Linux:** expected for Swift, CoreML, Tauri, and macOS window behavior. Use platform-neutral tests where appropriate and mark Mac verification outstanding.
- **Phone Remote tests pass but a phone cannot connect:** protocol tests do not establish firewall, camera handoff, local-network permission, or mobile-browser behavior. Follow the [offline remote checklist](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque/REMOTE_OFFLINE_CHECKLIST.md).
- **A parser change needs a new library:** inspect `src/lib/document-import/PARSERS.md` and retain bundled, local assets and third-party notices. Do not fetch a runtime CDN or render imported HTML.
- **A Flow test passes but a live Mac behaves differently:** accuracy, latency, resource use, microphone permission, CoreML/ANE behavior, helper cleanup, and the exact silence boundary require supported hardware.

Read next: [Requirements and installation](/guide/requirements-installation/), [Local Flow](/guide/local-flow/), or [Updating and uninstalling](/guide/updating-uninstalling/).
